interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is reported absent. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 81.76 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 65.41–98.11 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology is reassuring, showing "surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." The preoperative factors include a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological T2 stage. The absence of lymph node metastasis is a positive finding. Countervailing factors are limited by the documented findings; however, the absence of postoperative PSA makes biochemical recurrence assessment unknown. The status of nodal sampling is documented as "Nodes were sampled," which provides some staging information. Information that would revise the prognosis significantly would be the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory. A missing postoperative PSA prevents any assessment of biochemical recurrence.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology demonstrates favorable findings. The surgical pathology report indicates "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological stage pT2. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." These findings are reassuring, particularly the negative margins and absence of lymph node metastasis. Countervailing factors are limited as the seminal vesicles were not invaded and lymphovascular invasion was absent. Nodal sampling was performed, which provides some staging information. The preoperative PSA was 4.3. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing postoperative PSA or its subsequent trajectory is the primary factor that would revise the prognosis. The documented pathology suggests a low risk based on the surgical findings.
